entries.title: Detecting Tycoon 2FA AiTM attacks across Entra ID and Google Workspace
entries.description: Tycoon 2FA bypasses MFA on Entra ID and Google Workspace. We map telemetry fingerprints across both platforms, ship detection rules for both tiers, and contain incidents in under 10 seconds with Elastic Workflows.

entries.title: PHANTOMPULSE: anatomy of a hijackable blockchain-C2 RAT
entries.description: Elastic Security Labs presents a detailed reverse-engineering analysis of PHANTOMPULSE, the long-lived RAT delivered to crypto-sector victims through the REF6598 intrusion set.

entries.title: LABScon25 Replay | Breach Alpha: Trading on Cyber Fallout
entries.description: Mick Baccio and Scott Roberts examine whether public breach signals and market timing models can turn cyber incidents into actionable trading opportunities.

entries.title: Elastic Security MCP App: Interactive security operations inside your AI Tools
entries.description: Elastic Security is the first security vendor to ship an interactive UI in AI tools. Triage alerts, hunt threats, correlate attack chains, and open cases, all from inside your AI conversation.

entries.title: Flash Alert: EtherRat and TukTuk C2 End in The Gentleman Ransomware
entries.description: The EtherRAT malware family was first reported by Sysdig back in December 2025. At that time, the initial access vector was exploitation of CVE-2025-55182 (React2Shell) targeting Linux servers. In March 2026, a Windows variant campaign was reported by Atos, with their investigation showing evidence of activity going back to the previous December. In April, we […]

entries.title: Copy Fail and DirtyFrag: Linux Page Cache Bugs in the Wild
entries.description: This research analyzes the Linux kernel privilege escalation vulnerabilities Copy Fail and DirtyFrag, which exploit subtle page cache corruption bugs to create reliable paths to root access. Additionally, Elastic Security Labs is releasing detection logic for these vulnerabilities.

entries.title: Detecting Web Server Probing & Fuzzing in Traefik with Automated Cloudflare Response
entries.description: This article shows how a customized Elastic Security ES|QL detection rule can identify web server probing and fuzzing activity in Traefik logs and automatically block the attacking IP via Cloudflare.

entries.title: PCPJack | Cloud Worm Evicts TeamPCP and Steals Credentials at Scale
entries.description: Cloud attack framework skips cryptomining, harvests financial, messaging, and enterprise credentials for fraud, spam, and potential extortion.

entries.title: TCLBANKER: Brazilian Banking Trojan Spreading via WhatsApp and Outlook
entries.description: REF3076 uses a trojanized Logitech installer to deploy TCLBANKER, a Brazilian banking trojan with environment-gated payloads, WPF fraud overlays, and self-propagating WhatsApp and Outlook worm modules.

entries.title: Your UEBA is lying to you: Why entity record quality decides everything
entries.description: Most entity analytics systems are confidently wrong. They track users who do not exist, generate risk scores built on noise, and call it behavioral analytics. Learn why the entities records you don't create matter as much as the ones you do and how a confidence-tiered model changes the game.

entries.title: AI-generated hunting leads: The hunt starts before you ask the question
entries.description: Introducing AI-generated hunting leads, proactive, environment-aware threat hypotheses powered by Elastic Entity analytics and integrated AI reasoning.

entries.title: Know who to watch before the incident finds you
entries.description: Elastic Security v9.4 introduces Entity Analytics Watchlists, a way to codify what your team already knows about high-risk entities and feed that context directly into risk scoring, without custom pipelines or detection engineering overhead

entries.title: Elastic Workflows GA: automation where your security data already lives
entries.description: Elastic Workflows is generally available in 9.4, bringing production-ready security automation with deeper case management integration, human-in-the-loop support, natural language authoring, and more.

entries.title: One agent, the right skills: Elastic Security 9.4 brings domain expertise on demand to every SOC workflow
entries.description: Elastic Security 9.4 introduces skills, modular AI capabilities that teach the Elastic AI Agent how to detect, investigate, and hunt like a specialist. This is how they work, and why they matter for the SOC.

entries.title: Elastic Conversational Entity Analytics: threat hunting in a single conversation
entries.description: Conversational Entity Analytics delivers Entity Analytics features as rich inline attachments and Canvas previews into Agent Builder, so you don’t have to leave the conversation.

entries.title: From plain English to production rule: AI-native Elasticsearch ES|QL detection in Elastic Security
entries.description: Elastic Security now lets analysts describe a threat behavior in plain language and receive a complete, validated Elasticsearch ES|QL detection rule in return, no query expertise required.

entries.title: DFIR: From alert to root cause using Osquery without leaving Elastic Security
entries.description: Learn how to perform distributed, real-time Digital Forensics and Incident Response (DFIR) using Osquery and Elastic to investigate threats at scale without relying on disk imaging.
